hypotheses.full_text: In a pediatric autism study using Harvard-Oxford cortical regions and thalamic seeds, functional connectivity was reported to be greater between the thalamus and superior temporal gyri. This is a population-level, cohort-specific hypothesis, not an individual diagnostic rule.
candidate_connections: Left Thalamus — Left Superior Temporal Gyrus, anterior division
hypotheses.mapping_basis: The feature-map CSV verifies both endpoint labels and numeric feature order; the study used Harvard-Oxford cortical/subcortical regions and reports bilateral superior temporal gyri. The study's whole superior temporal region and connectivity estimand are broader/different than this selected HO connection.
hypotheses.counterfactual_text: Counterfactual direction for model testing only: suppose functional connectivity between the thalamus and superior temporal gyri were lower in an autism cohort using Harvard-Oxford regions. This reversed direction is not the finding reported by Nair et al.

source.title: Regional specificity of aberrant thalamocortical connectivity in autism
source.population: Pediatric ASD and typically developing cohort; fMRI analysis final sample 37 ASD and 38 TD after motion exclusions
source.atlas: Harvard-Oxford cortical/subcortical structural atlases for cortical ROIs and thalamus
source.direction_evidence: The paper reports overconnectivity with bilateral superior temporal gyri; its sample and seed definitions limit direct transfer.
source.confidence_and_uncertainty: A real directional ASD group hypothesis with direct atlas-family compatibility; small sample, age-specific and not an individual-level diagnostic marker. One selected feature is eligible, so evidence coverage is 1/252 named connections.

intervention_only_negative_control.text: Counterfactual anatomy mismatch for intervention testing only: functional connectivity between the left thalamus and an occipital cortical region is altered in autism. This is not an ASD-specific evidence claim and is not eligible for training matches.
intervention_only_negative_control.counterfactual_text: Counterfactual reverse direction for the anatomy-mismatch intervention only: functional connectivity between the left thalamus and an occipital cortical region is altered in the opposite direction in autism. This is not an ASD-specific evidence claim and is not eligible for training matches.

non_edge_level_sources.title: Multiscale heterogeneity of atypical functional connectivity in autism
non_edge_level_sources.use: Motivates individual-level rejection/uncertainty; network-scale Schaefer findings are not mapped to individual selected Harvard-Oxford connections.

non_edge_level_sources.use: Methodological motivation for real ROI-anchored prompts; its AAL claims are not transferred to this atlas.

non_edge_level_sources.use: Methodological context only; not used as evidence for a specific ASD connection direction.
